name: Visitor
intent: Add new operations to a set of classes without modifying them, by moving each operation into its own visitor object.
scenario: Shapes (circles, rectangles) need operations like area, perimeter and a text description. New operations keep being requested, but the shape classes should stay untouched.
problem: Every new operation (area, perimeter, export...) would add a method to every shape class. Shapes bloat with unrelated code. The alternative, a function full of instanceof checks (runtime type tests), forgets new shape types silently.
solution: Give each shape one accept(visitor) method that calls back visitCircle(this) or visitRectangle(this). Each operation becomes a Visitor class with one method per shape type. This double dispatch picks the right code for the shape and the operation. New operations are new visitors; shapes never change.
pain: Each new operation means a new method on every shape
Shape classes fill up with unrelated operations
The alternative, instanceof chains, silently skips new shapes
Operations are scattered across the shape classes
benefits: A new operation is a new visitor, with no shape edits
Each operation's code is in one place
The compiler (in a statically typed language) flags a visitor that forgets a shape
whenToUse: You have a stable set of element types and many operations over them
Operations should stay out of the element classes
Compilers and tree walkers: syntax trees, document structures, export formats
whenNotToUse: The set of element types changes often: every visitor must change with it
There are only one or two operations: put them in the classes
Elements' internals are not accessible enough for the visitor to do its job
pitfalls: Adding a new shape means updating every visitor
Double dispatch is confusing the first time you meet it
Visitors may need public access to element internals, weakening encapsulation
Verbose: an interface method per element type

roles.label: Visitor
roles.description: Interface with one visit method per element type.

roles.label: Concrete Visitor
roles.description: One operation, implemented across all element types.

roles.label: Concrete Element
roles.description: A shape that calls the matching visit method.

quiz.question: A drawing app has Circle, Rectangle and Triangle classes that have been stable for years. Product asks for a new operation, a text description of each shape, and wants the shape classes left alone. With the Visitor pattern, what changes?
options: Write one new Visitor class, leaving the shapes as they are
Add a describe() method to each of the three shape classes and call it directly
Add a describe parameter to accept() on every shape so each can handle it itself
Subclass each shape into a describing version that overrides the draw logic
quiz.explanation: Every shape already has accept(visitor) and calls back the matching visit method, so a new operation is only a new visitor. Adding methods or subclasses edits or multiplies the shapes.

quiz.question: A compiler has 10 syntax tree node types and 6 visitors: type check, print, optimise, and so on. The team adds an 11th node, Ternary. In a language with an interface method per node type, what happens?
options: Nothing, visitors only handle known node types
Only the node's accept() needs writing, the visitors inherit the rest
Only the optimiser needs updating, the others read the tree generically
All 6 visitors must gain a visit method for Ternary
quiz.explanation: A new element type touches every visitor, which is the main cost of Visitor. The interface method per type makes forgetting one a compile error. Nothing is inherited for free, since each visitor method does different work.

quiz.question: A plugin system lets third parties add new document element types every month, while only three operations (render, validate, export) exist and rarely change. A developer proposes Visitor for the operations. What is the best judgment?
options: Visitor fits, as long as the visitors use reflection to handle unknown elements
Visitor fits, because the three operations are stable and few in number
Poor fit: put the operations on each element as methods and let polymorphism dispatch it
Visitor fits if each visitor ends with a default branch that ignores unknown elements
quiz.explanation: Visitor suits a stable set of element types with many growing operations. Here it is the reverse, so each new element would force changes in all visitors. Reflection or a silent default hide missing handling, which is the instanceof-chain flaw again.
